mcqs.question: Which of the following compound statements is logically equivalent to the biconditional statement (P ↔ Q)?
mcqs.explanation: The biconditional P ↔ Q is true when both statements have the same truth value, i.e., both true or both false. This condition is captured by (P ∧ Q) ∨ (¬P ∧ ¬Q). Options B and C represent exclusive or and a different combination, while D is a disjunction of implications, not equivalent to the biconditional.

mcqs.question: Consider the compound statement (P ∨ Q) → (¬P ∧ R). Using a truth table, what is the truth value of the statement when P is True, Q is False, and R is True?
mcqs.explanation: With P = T and Q = F, (P ∨ Q) is True. ¬P is False, so (¬P ∧ R) = False ∧ True = False. An implication True → False is False. Hence the statement is false. Options A, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: In logical connectives, the conjunction of two statements P and Q, denoted by P ∧ Q, is true ____.

options.A: only when both P and Q are true
options.B: when at least one of P or Q is true
options.C: only when both P and Q are false
options.D: when P is true and Q is false

mcqs.answer: only when both P and Q are true
mcqs.explanation: Conjunction (AND) requires both component statements to be true for the whole compound statement to be true. All other options describe disjunction, negation, or a specific false case.

mcqs.question: The logical disjunction of statements P and Q, written as P ∨ Q, is true ____.

options.A: only when both P and Q are true
options.B: when at least one of P or Q is true
options.C: only when both P and Q are false
options.D: when P is false and Q is true

mcqs.answer: when at least one of P or Q is true
mcqs.explanation: Disjunction (OR) is true if either P, Q, or both are true. It is false only when both are false. Option D describes a specific true case but does not capture the full definition, while A and C are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the implication P → Q and distinguishes it from conjunction P ∧ Q?

options.A: P → Q is true except when P is true and Q is false; P ∧ Q is true only when both are true.
options.B: P → Q is true only when both P and Q are true; P ∧ Q is true except when P is true and Q is false.
options.C: P → Q and P ∧ Q have identical truth tables.
options.D: P → Q is true only when P is false; P ∧ Q is true only when Q is false.

mcqs.answer: P → Q is true except when P is true and Q is false; P ∧ Q is true only when both are true.
mcqs.explanation: Implication is false only in the case T → F; otherwise it is true. Conjunction requires both operands to be true. Options B, C, and D misstate the truth conditions.

mcqs.question: The statement "The alarm rings if and only if the door is opened" can be expressed as which of the following logical forms?
mcqs.explanation: "If and only if" denotes a biconditional, which is equivalent to the conjunction of two implications: Alarm → Door and Door → Alarm. Options B and C represent simple OR and AND, while D is only one direction.

mcqs.question: Given the compound statement (P ∧ Q) → (R ∨ ¬S), which of the following rows of its truth table makes the whole statement false?

options.A: P = T, Q = T, R = F, S = T
options.B: P = F, Q = T, R = F, S = F
options.C: P = T, Q = F, R = T, S = T
options.D: P = F, Q = F, R = T, S = F

mcqs.answer: P = T, Q = T, R = F, S = T
mcqs.explanation: The implication is false only when its antecedent (P ∧ Q) is true and its consequent (R ∨ ¬S) is false. In option A, P ∧ Q = T and R ∨ ¬S = F ∨ F = F, so the whole statement is false. All other options have a false antecedent or a true consequent, making the implication true.

mcqs.question: A student will receive a scholarship only if she scores above 90% in mathematics and above 85% in physics. Which logical expression correctly represents the condition for receiving the scholarship?
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "and" indicates that both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously, which is represented by the conjunction (M > 90) ∧ (P > 85). Option B uses disjunction, C is a one‑way implication, and D denotes a biconditional, none of which capture the required "both" condition.
